title: Skip counting with equal hops

explain.say: Have you ever counted socks in pairs? 2, 4, 6, 8! That is skip counting. Look at the number line: the frog starts at 0 and takes jumps of 2, skipping the numbers in between, all the way to 20.
Watch each hop from 0: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and on to 20. That is 10 equal hops of 2. Every number it lands on is even. Which number comes after 12?
Now jumps of 5, starting at 0: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is how you count fingers, one hand at a time. How many hops of 5 reach 25?
Now giant jumps of 10 from 0: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Just 5 hops reach 50! Counting in 10s helps you count 10-cent or 10-rupee coins fast. What comes after 50?
Fantastic skipping! Here is the wow: skip counting is secret times tables. Look at hops of 3 from 0: 3, 6, 9, all the way to 30. That is 10 threes. Can you count in 3s without looking?

faq.a: Skip counting means counting forward by the same number each time, skipping the numbers in between. Counting 2, 4, 6, 8 is skip counting in 2s.
Start at 0 and add 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. The numbers always end in 5 or 0.
Lots of things come in pairs, like socks, shoes and eyes. Counting in 2s is twice as fast as counting in 1s.

faq.q: How is skip counting like times tables?
faq.a: Each hop is one more group. 4 hops of 5 land on 20, and 4 times 5 is 20. Skip counting builds the times tables.
asks: Is skip counting the same as multiplying?

faq.q: What pattern is in counting in 10s?
faq.a: Counting in 10s from 0, every number ends in 0, and the tens digit goes up by 1 each time: 10, 20, 30, 40.
asks: Why do the 10s all end in 0?

facts: Counting in 2s from 0 lands only on even numbers.
Counting in 5s from 0, every number ends in 5 or 0.

wrong.2: 25 skips a hop; it comes after 20.

quiz.say: How many hops of 10 from 0 reach 60?

wrong.0: 60 is where you land, not the number of hops.
